notes.fact: Kyiv Independent says the death toll from the Russian strike on Komyshuvakha reached 53 on the fifth day of search work. It calls this the deadliest attack on Zaporizhzhia region of the war.
AP reports Russian guided bombs hit a school and shelter in Komyshuvakha on Nov 2. Ukrainian officials had confirmed 37 deaths by Nov 4, with about 38 more possibly trapped.

Moscow Times says Russian attacks caused outages in seven Ukrainian regions, including Kyiv and Kharkiv. Ukraine's deputy energy minister said the capital region was worst hit and the grid was partly shut down.

Anadolu reports Ukraine's General Staff counted two missiles and 128 drones overnight, 105 downed. Russia's defence ministry claimed 496 Ukrainian drones destroyed. The outlet says independent verification is difficult.
notes.key: claim:ukraine general staff and russian defence
notes.claim_by: party:Ukraine General Staff and Russian defence ministry

notes.fact: TASS, Russian state media, says Russia's defence ministry reported a massive overnight strike on military-industrial, energy and transport targets in Kyiv and its region.
notes.event: Russian strike on Kyiv region Nov 7

notes.fact: Zelensky says Ukrainian intelligence expects a new Russian strike on energy sites, Dnipro bridges and civilian infrastructure. He asked partners to speed up Patriot interceptor deliveries.
Reuters reports a six-day local ceasefire around Russian-held Oleshky held to its last day. Fighting and long-range air attacks continued elsewhere along the front.
Russia's defence ministry says it hit a dry cargo ship carrying supplies for Ukraine's military southeast of Odesa. It named no vessel or flag, and damage is unknown.
notes.event: Russian claim of ship hit off Odesa

notes.fact: The tanker Mentor, hit by a Russian drone off Odesa on Sept 24, broke free of its tow. Romania rescued three tug crew; Bulgaria is monitoring the drifting vessel.
US officials told CBS the US made limited defensive strikes on Qeshm Island after Iran's Revolutionary Guards fired at a US jet. They also said Iran fired a missile that threatened shipping.
Al Jazeera says Trump confirmed strikes on an Iranian anti-aircraft site. Iranian media said Qeshm was hit. Iran's security council chief Rezaei called the US reply on Hormuz 'unconvincing'.
Outlook India says explosions were heard on Qeshm, Hengam and near Bandar Abbas. It says it found no public CENTCOM or Pentagon statement confirming the operation.
NBC says Trump stated the US carried out new limited strikes on an Iranian air defence system on Friday. It is the first action since the midterms.
Al Jazeera reports the IRGC says it shot down a US MQ-1 over Qeshm and that two tankers hit mines on Friday. Another tanker reported an explosion.
notes.event: IRGC drone claims and Hormuz tankers

notes.fact: Al Jazeera says Iran warns it will respond more widely than before if the US resumes the war. It says states aiding the US would be legitimate targets.
Al Jazeera cites an Iranian lawmaker saying ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar may pass Hormuz. It cites IMO and UKMTO data: over 120 ships hit, October worst month.
Al Jazeera's Iran page says Qatar urged the US and Iran to settle the war without waiting for a perfect moment. It also reports Trump claiming a lot of progress in talks.
CBS reports Qatar and Pakistan are mediating. Iran says it will reopen Hormuz only if the US meets seven conditions. Trump said a deal still could happen.
Al Jazeera notes US media, citing officials, said Central Command prepared strikes that could start as early as Nov 4, with three US carriers in the region.
notes.event: Possible resumed US strikes after midterms

notes.fact: AP reports two officials said Netanyahu pushed Trump for strikes in a weekend call. Iran's new supreme leader told commanders to answer any threat immediately, without geographic limits.
notes.event: Possible resumed US strikes after midterms

notes.fact: IBTimes, citing Reuters, says Houthi forces are within about 50 miles of Aden, closer than any time since 2015. The gains threaten the Aden-Taiz route.

South Front, a Russia-linked outlet, says Houthis took al-Maqatirah in Lahij on Nov 2. It lists Houthi-claimed strikes on Riyadh (Nov 4) and Dammam (Nov 5) airports; the coalition says it intercepted a missile toward Medina.
Türkiye Today, citing the Wall Street Journal, says Houthis told Riyadh a halt would cost $51 billion plus recognition as Yemen's rulers. The report says Saudi Arabia asked what a halt would take.
notes.event: Houthi price for ending Saudi attacks

notes.fact: Sudan Tribune reports an RSF drone strike killed five and wounded 47 at a Kordofan University dormitory in El Obeid, per Sudanese Doctors Network. No newer El Obeid report found in this search.
notes.event: RSF drone strikes on El Obeid

notes.fact: AFRICOM lists an airstrike against al-Shabaab on Oct 19, coordinated with Somalia's government. It gave no casualty figures.
AFRICOM says it struck al-Shabaab on Oct 17 near Dhooble Airport, about 180 km northwest of Kismayo. It names no units or assets.
Reuters reports Seoul says North Korea fired multiple missiles from Sondok toward the east-coast sea, its fourth launch in a month. Kim Yo Jong ruled out dialogue with Washington.
KCNA, North Korean state media, says the Nov 4 launch tested a new anti-aircraft missile, plus a cruise-missile drill against a simulated airfield.
Seoul's Joint Chiefs believe the missiles flew under 300 km and do not rule out a short-range ballistic missile, per Yonhap.
notes.claim_by: party:South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff

notes.fact: AP says tension has grown since September mine blasts wounded South Korean soldiers. North Korea threatened to resume loudspeakers and deploy weapons near the border. It denies the US-claimed $6.3bn Binance hack.
notes.event: DMZ tension and Binance heist attribution

notes.fact: Asia News Network says fire over a disputed Torkham check post shut the crossing, and one civilian died in mortar fire near Angoor Adda. Pakistan's military warned Kabul of 'punishment'.
FDD says Taliban and Pakistani forces clashed at least three times since Oct 19. The Taliban claim Pakistani drones hit Paktika; Pakistan calls that account a fabrication.
France 24 says Nov 1 air strikes killed 12 and injured 32 in Rakhine. It says the military began an offensive on Sept 4 to retake the state, about 90% held by the Arakan Army.
Anadolu, citing The Irrawaddy, reports at least 15 civilians killed across Rakhine and Karenni states, including three children bombed at a Loikaw school on Saturday.
The Arakan Army-aligned Global Arakan Network says a jet bombed Nan Kyar village in Mrauk-U on Nov 5, killing a pregnant woman and injuring over 10. Unverified.
News.az says the Arakan Army holds most of Rakhine and has advanced toward Sittwe. It says casualty figures are unverified and the government made no comment.

Latin Times says Salvadoran forces began their first large ground operation in Plaine du Cul-de-Sac on Nov 2, reportedly killing at least a dozen gang fighters. Over 2,000 Salvadoran troops are now deployed.
Al Jazeera says Haitian police found the burned truck of four Salvadoran technicians missing since an Oct 18 ambush, but not the men. Bukele posted videos of troops patrolling.
CNN, citing AP, says gangs fired on a Salvadoran armored vehicle on Oct 18, leaving four soldiers unaccounted for. The US UN ambassador condemned the attack.
notes.key: claim:salvadoran military and us ambassador to un
notes.claim_by: party:Salvadoran military and US ambassador to UN
